edges.reason: The actual computational rule can be stated piecewise and gives both solutions of |x|=a for a positive a. Gemini treats the geometry/definition node as unavoidable, but this geometry-specific endpoint is not needed to apply that supplied rule.
edges.scope: Geometric distance interpretation as preparation for the piecewise absolute-value computation rule

edges.reason: The stated rule for a negative input returns its opposite; solving |x|=a also identifies the opposite pair.
The target explicitly also compares on a number line. That supplies a valid alternative to absolute-value computation, so Gemini overstates one permitted negative-comparison method as necessary.
edges.scope: Comparing two negative numbers by their absolute values

edges.reason: The description names this route, while the stated criteria also cover like denominators and like numerators directly. Common-numerator or other valid comparisons avoid the common-denominator procedure. Keep the explicitly described method locally rather than require it for every fraction comparison; minimum-common-multiple efficiency is not required by this edge.
edges.scope: Comparing unlike-denominator fractions by an explicitly chosen common-denominator rewriting route

edges.reason: The target compares how many equal units or how large each unit is; reduction to coprime terms is not a component. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: The equal-part, numerator and denominator meanings used to compare like numerators or denominators

edges.reason: The criterion explicitly asks for the least common multiple of the denominators. An arbitrary product denominator would not meet that extra criterion.
Renaming fractions with a common denominator preserves value by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same factor.
edges.scope: rewriting fractions with a new denominator
